Computing ${B}^{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 25 \\ -1 & -5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 & 25 \\ -1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =O.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that, since ${B}^{2}=O,$ the matrix $B$ is a nilpotent matrix of index $2.$ 

We can use this fact to compute ${B}^{6}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{6} & ={B}^{2}\cdot {B}^{4} \\  & =O\cdot {B}^{4} \\  & =O\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{B}^{6}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
